Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Full Text

ranked.title: Personal Income and Outlays, April 2026
ranked.why_it_matters: Personal income decreased less than $0.1 billion (less than 0.1 percent at a monthly rate) in April, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Disposable personal income (DPI)-personal income less personal current taxes-decreased $19.9 billion (0.1 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $111.1 billion (0.5 percent). Personal outlays-the sum of PCE, personal interest payments, and personal current transfer payments-increased $114.0 billion in April. Personal saving was $611.7 billion in April, and the personal saving rate-personal saving as a percentage of DPI-was 2.6 percent. Full Text

ranked.title: Personal Income and Outlays, January 2026

Personal saving was $1.05 trillion in January, and the personal saving rate-personal saving as a percentage of disposable personal income-was 4.5 percent. Full Text

The fourth-quarter deficit was 2.4 percent of current-dollar gross domestic product, down from 3.1 percent in the third quarter.The U.S. net international investment position, the difference between U.S. residents' foreign financial assets and liabilities, was -$27.54 trillion at the end of the fourth quarter of 2025. Assets totaled $42.96 trillion, and liabilities totaled $70.49 trillion. At the end of the third quarter, the net investment position was -$27.55 trillion (revised). Full Text

ranked.title: Direct Investment by Country and Industry, 2024
ranked.why_it_matters: The U.S. direct investment abroad position, or cumulative level of investment, increased $206.3 billion to $6.83 trillion at the end of 2024, according to statistics released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. The foreign direct investment in the United States position increased $332.1 billion to $5.71 trillion at the end of 2024. By industry, affiliates in manufacturing increased the most. Full Text
